product_from_film: Runable is presented as a general AI agent for reports, decks, websites and other tasks.
explains_well: A running-barrier metaphor connects personal ambition with the wish to remove routine work.
unclear: The film spends most of its time on motivation and frustration, then shows only brief prompts and output cards without a complete task.
scenario: A frustrated builder asks for reports and decks while other work requests accumulate.

categories.finding: Historical barrier → personal expectations → building frustration → agent outputs → running call to action.
Huge 1954 text and an archival-looking portrait establish history rather than software.
The product capabilities first appear at 52s; the report/deck workflow is brief at 79–83s.
Large numbers turn/change scale, text layers accumulate and output cards float around a laptop. Exact paths/easing unverified.
Archive/color alternation links the old runner with the modern character; black text interruptions mark emotional turns.
Grainy monochrome, warm low-light work scenes, red track and dark UI create distinct phases.
Large words and numbers dominate; work requests are concrete, but final output panels are brief and small.
ASR supports a motivational narrative with a short product offer; delivery is not assessed.
Music character and structure are unverified.
Effects and their sources are unverified.
categories.reason: No validated listening; waveform peaks do not identify effects.

categories.finding: Sound sync is unverified.
categories.reason: No validated listening or paired audiovisual timing.

categories.finding: Archival-looking sports, portraits, modern character scenes, UI and a motivational excerpt are combined; provenance unknown.
Source duration 100.309 s; Watch metadata 1440 × 1080. Frame rate, audio clipping and export quality not checked here.
categories.reason: Parent source metadata supports duration and dimensions; visual review is sampled.

categories.finding: Visible captions convey ambition and frustration; request/output cards and final labels identify an agent, but no complete task is readable.
Faces and oversized text dominate until the late prompt/output sequence.
About three quarters of the film precedes the concrete work-request sequence, leaving little time to inspect outputs.
The running analogy returns at the end; the work-barrier promise has only a montage payoff.
The edit appears designed to move from aspiration through anger to agency; no audience effect is measured.
The modern runner and repeated Bannister imagery hold the metaphor together; the three output tasks are not traced individually.
Historical claims, broad agent competence, task completion and output quality are unverified. Selected UI states do not prove execution.
Running links the name and narrative; the report/deck/site examples need more depth to distinguish the agent.
Give one result more space.
categories.experiment: Shorten the archive opening and show the market report request, source work and final report section.

categories.finding: Use a recurring physical metaphor around a complete task.
